activities.title: Two kinds of information
activities.instruction: Understand why route-specific data can belong near the route that owns the screen, and distinguish route data from local UI state.

content.title: Route Data Belongs Near the Route
content.context:
Some information describes the screen itself:

```text
product 42
```

Other information is local UI behavior:

```text
is the review form open?
is the help popover open?
```

The first group is often part of the route's application data. The second group is local interaction state.
goals: Understand why route-specific data can belong near the route that owns the screen, and distinguish route data from local UI state.

content.title: Route-owned data
content.text:
A route for `/products/42` needs the product with id `42`.

A clean mental model is:

```text
route
  ↓
identify resource
  ↓
load data
  ↓
render screen
```

Some routing libraries provide route-level loaders or similar mechanisms for this. React Router currently provides route loaders and exposes their results to the matched route components.

content.question:
A route `/teams/12` needs team `12` before rendering its main content.

Which boundary is the strongest candidate for loading the team data?

options.text: An unrelated button component deep in the screen.
The route or route-level data boundary responsible for the team screen.

feedback.correct: Route-specific data belongs near the route that owns the screen. This gives the application a clear place to coordinate data needed for that location.
feedback.incorrect: Route-specific data belongs near the route that owns the screen. This gives the application a clear place to coordinate data needed for that location.

activities.title: Loading and error states belong to the data boundary

content.title: Loading and error states belong to the data boundary
content.text:
If the team data is not ready yet, the application needs a loading state.

If the request fails, it needs an error state.

That gives a simple route lifecycle:

```text
match route
   ↓
start data work
   ↓
loading
   ↓
 ┌───────────────┐
 │               │
 success       failure
 │               │
render data    render recovery
```

The important skill is not memorizing a library API. It is deciding **which boundary owns the data and therefore owns the states around that data**.

activities.title: Do not duplicate remote data in every child

content.question:
Suppose a route has a product and five child components all independently request the same product.

What problem can that create?

options.text: It duplicates responsibility and makes the data flow harder to understand.
It removes the need for errors.

feedback.correct: Shared route data should generally have an identifiable owner instead of being requested independently by every child.
feedback.incorrect: Shared route data should generally have an identifiable owner instead of being requested independently by every child.

takeaways: **Mental model:** Put data ownership near the boundary that owns the screen that needs it.
